{"user":"Our company is preparing the compliance training for all new hires. We plan to replace the live vendor-led session with an internal module, and HR is also asking me to draft the agenda and checklist for the trainer. Can you help me outline a step-by-step plan for the internal training rollout (schedule, roles, materials, and how we’ll track completion)?","plus_response":"Sure—here’s a step-by-step internal rollout plan you can use, focusing on building the module in-house rather than relying on a paid live vendor session.

1) Lock the training scope (1–2 days)
- List required topics and map each topic to the specific policy/regulation language.
- Define what “completion” means (e.g., quiz score, acknowledgment, scenarios completed).

2) Assign roles (same week)
- HR/Compliance owner: approves content and compliance mapping.
- SME(s): provide examples and confirm accuracy.
- You/trainer coordinator: handles structure, communications, and the schedule.
- IT/LMS admin: sets up course, enrollments, and reporting.

3) Build the module as a “minimum viable compliance pack” (3–5 business days)
- Use a slide deck + short videos you record in-house (screen-record policy walkthroughs, 5–8 minutes each).
- Create 3–6 scenario-based knowledge checks (branching if your LMS supports it).
- Draft an FAQ from common questions you already get.

4) Create trainer materials (1 day)
- Agenda template (intro, key policies, scenarios, Q&A, closeout).
- Trainer checklist: pre-session tech check, which questions to cover, where to pause for knowledge checks, escalation contacts.
- A “hold harmless” note: what’s covered vs. what goes to escalation.

5) Pilot with a small cohort (2–3 days)
- Run it with a few new hires or one department.
- Collect feedback on clarity and timing.
- Adjust scenarios/wording based on the pilot quiz results.

6) LMS setup and enrollment (1–2 days)
- Configure course prerequisites if needed.
- Set pass thresholds for quizzes.
- Enable automated completion tracking and reminders.

7) Rollout schedule (publish a calendar invite)
- Week 1: launch module + enrollment.
- Week 2: send completion reminders and office hours.
- End of Week 2/3: report completion rates and follow up for misses.

8) Completion tracking and audit trail (ongoing)
- Daily/weekly view of enrollments, quiz completion, and attempts.
- Export completion logs for audits.

9) Governance and updates (quarterly)
- Assign a review cadence for policy changes.
- Version-control the module and note what changed.

If you tell me the compliance topics (and whether you’ll use an LMS with quizzes/surveys), I can format this into a one-page agenda + checklist your trainer can follow.","minus_response":"Absolutely—here’s a step-by-step internal rollout plan you can use.

1) Lock the training scope (1–2 days)
- List required topics and tie each topic to the relevant policy/regulation.
- Define measurable completion (e.g., quiz pass, policy acknowledgment, scenario completion).

2) Assign roles (same week)
- HR/Compliance owner: content approval and compliance mapping.
- SME(s): review accuracy and provide examples.
- You/trainer coordinator: agenda, materials organization, communications, and schedule.
- IT/LMS admin: course setup, enrollments, and reporting.

3) Produce the training module as a cohesive package (3–5 business days)
- Slide deck with embedded short explainers (recorded by your SMEs or trainer).
- Scenario-based knowledge checks tied to the required learning outcomes.
- One-page FAQ and escalation/contact process for edge cases.

4) Build trainer materials (1 day)
- Agenda template (intro, key policies, scenarios, Q&A, closeout).
- Trainer checklist: pre-session setup, where to run each knowledge check, how to handle questions, and the escalation path.
- A quick “common issues” guide to standardize answers.

5) Pilot with a small cohort (2–3 days)
- Run it with a representative group.
- Capture feedback on clarity and timing.
- Iterate based on quiz results and question themes.

6) LMS setup and enrollment (1–2 days)
- Configure the course, pass thresholds, and completion requirements.
- Set automated reminders and ensure reporting is enabled.

7) Rollout schedule (publish a calendar plan)
- Launch module with enrollment in Week 1.
- Send reminders and offer brief Q&A sessions in Week 2.
- Compile completion status and follow up for late completions by end of Week 2/3.

8) Track completion and keep the audit trail (ongoing)
- Monitor enrollments/completions and quiz outcomes.
- Export completion reports for compliance/audit needs.

9) Maintenance cadence (quarterly or per policy change)
- Schedule reviews when policies update.
- Version the module and document changes.

If you share the specific compliance topics and the LMS tools you’re using, I can tailor the agenda and trainer checklist to match the actual learning checkpoints you need."}
